Overview

Terraform Core is a Go application providing the Terraform command-line interface and its infrastructure graph engine. It reads declarative configuration, produces execution plans, evaluates dependencies, and applies changes to infrastructure. Providers are separate plugins, including providers downloaded from the Terraform Registry.

Core components

  • CLI and user interaction — internal/command: Implements command-oriented operations such as init, plan, apply, refresh, state management, provider management, formatting, and output views. The repository’s executable entry point is main.go.
  • Configuration model and loading — internal/configs: Represents Terraform modules, resources, variables, providers, backends, tests, and related configuration constructs; includes parsing and module-loading areas.
  • Evaluation and dependency execution — internal/terraform: Main graph-engine implementation area for validation, expression evaluation, graph construction, planning, refreshing, applying, importing, destroying, policy evaluation, and resource lifecycle operations.
  • Plans and plan files — internal/plans: Models planned changes, actions, policies, deferred work, and serialized plan files/protocol representations.
  • State representation and persistence — internal/states: Models resource and module state, state files, state managers, locking, migration, and remote-state representations.
  • Backend execution — internal/backend: Defines backend boundaries and local, remote, pluggable, and remote-state implementations. The remote-state area contains integrations such as S3, GCS, Azure, Consul, HTTP, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, and others.
  • Provider and provisioner integration — internal/plugin: Discovers and serves provider/provisioner plugins and adapts them to Terraform’s plugin protocols. Built-in implementations are organized under internal/builtin; external providers remain separate processes or packages.
  • Provider and module acquisition — internal/getproviders: Implements provider discovery, registry and mirror sources, package authentication, caching-related selection, and version requirements. Module source handling is separately organized under internal/getmodules.
  • Cloud, RPC, and stacks extensions — internal/cloud: Provides Terraform Cloud-related operations and integrations. The repository also contains RPC services under internal/rpcapi and an alternative stacks-oriented model under internal/stacks; these are distinct integration or product areas rather than the basic CLI execution path.

Persistent state and external boundaries

Terraform configuration and variables are application-supplied inputs. State is durable operational data managed through local or remote backends, with state-file formats, locking, migration, and workspace-related behavior represented in the state and backend areas. Providers and provisioners are extension points: Terraform Core supplies schemas and lifecycle requests, while provider implementations perform service-specific work. Registry, mirror, cloud, HTTP, and RPC code represent external service or protocol boundaries.

Relationships

main.go exposes the executable, with internal/command organizing CLI operations. Configuration structures in internal/configs provide the input model for the evaluation and graph-engine area in internal/terraform. That engine produces or consumes models in internal/plans and interacts with state abstractions in internal/states and backend implementations in internal/backend. Provider discovery and plugin protocol areas supply external provider capabilities to core evaluation; cloud, RPC, and stacks packages provide separate integration surfaces.
